summary: CGM coverage and profile completeness were strong enough for review. The clearest pattern is recurrent hypoglycemia risk overnight and in the late evening, alongside sustained daytime hyperglycemia from late morning through afternoon. Because carb logging is absent and most therapy-response windows are correction- and automation-confounded, no single basal, CR, or ISF change is well supported yet.

analysis_steps.findings: 14 days of Nightscout data had 98.7% CGM coverage, no invalid or duplicate entries, and 5-minute cadence with only short gaps. The active AAPS profile is present and authoritative for review under profile_context.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 CGM entries, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, last entry close to period end, selected_profile_id matches the authoritative aaps_profile.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carb entries or meal labels, so meal timing cannot be validated from telemetry alone.

analysis_steps.findings: Hypoglycemia is the main safety constraint, with repeated lows to 41-42 mg/dL and total time below range of 5.1%. Hyperglycemia also appears, with highs up to 286-293 mg/dL and time above range of 8.9%.
analysis_steps.evidence: Glucose extremes and summary metrics show both low and high excursions; CV is 32.6%.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Constrained by the available CGM signal and by the inability to separate meal, correction, and automation effects perfectly.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal annotations or fasting-only windows to determine whether lows are basal-, correction-, or activity-related.

analysis_steps.findings: Local-time glucose is lowest overnight and around early morning, while late morning through afternoon shows the highest averages and the most time above range. Basal and target segments are plausible but not isolated from meals, corrections, temp targets, sensor/site changes, or IOB.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local shows lower averages around 00:00-02:00 and higher averages around 10:00-16:00; targets are 90 overnight, 100 from 08:00, then 90 at 23:00; basal steps are 0.5-0.8 U/h.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on safety_overview and on separating confounders before attributing pattern to basal.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No event-light fasting windows and no carb logs, so basal excess or deficit cannot be proven from current data.

analysis_steps.findings: CR, ISF, and DIA are fully declared, but the record lacks carb entries and has only correction-heavy response windows. That makes CR and ISF validation weak, and DIA cannot be isolated from automation behavior.
analysis_steps.evidence: CR segments vary by time, ISF is 56 mg/dL/U, DIA is 10 h, and therapy_response_windows show mixed 2-6 hour outcomes with confounding from corrections and automation.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on basal_targets and safety_overview; interpretation is limited by absent meal documentation.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal carb data, no prebolus timing, and no clean isolated correction or meal tests.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM settings are internally coherent. SMB is enabled, UAM is enabled, SMB is allowed with temp targets, and SMB is intentionally not enabled with COB or after carbs, so UAM is not duplicating COB counting.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true, smb_with_cob_enabled=false, smb_after_carbs_enabled=false, smb_with_temp_target_enabled=true, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled=false; loop messages show SMB/UAM operating within normal closed-loop response.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on the safety context from CHECKPOINT 1 and on the absence of carb logs from the analysis.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carb entries and no fasting windows, so it is not possible to prove whether SMB/UAM is compensating for basal, CR, or meal timing rather than causing a defect.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic sensitivity is active even though autosens_enabled is false, and sensitivity_ratio around 1 is a neutral adjustment rather than evidence of disabled automation. Max basal 12 U/h and max IOB 25 U do not appear binding in the observed range.
analysis_steps.evidence: dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70%, autosens_raises_target=false, autosens_lowers_target=false; observed enacted temp basals stay well below the max basal ceiling, and IOB values remain far below the max IOB limit.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on SMB/UAM review and on the unresolved meal-vs-correction distinction.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No clean isolated sensitivity tests and no meal logs, so the system cannot be cleanly separated into basal, meal, and sensitivity components.

analysis_steps.findings: There is no declared typical meal strategy in analysis_context, and telemetry contains no carb entries. Therefore no reliable prebolus timing or immediate bolus percentage can be inferred from the package. The day-time highs may reflect meal timing or absorption, but the record cannot separate that from basal or automation effects.
analysis_steps.evidence: analysis_context.meal_strategies is empty and strategy_stable_for_period is null; carb_treatment_entries are empty; therapy_response_windows are dominated by correction boluses with mixed later outcomes.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on basal_targets, profile_cr_isf_dia, automation_smb_uam, and automation_sensitivity_limits.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal carb amounts, no meal timestamps, and no per-meal bolus execution details.

analysis_steps.findings: No regular carb entries and no extended-carb entries are present, so e-carbs are not supported as a recurring pattern from this dataset. Nothing in the package justifies equating e-carbs with an extended pump bolus.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_treatment_entries=0, extended_carb_entries=0, and no declared e-carb strategy in analysis_context.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on meal_bolus_strategy and the absence of meal-linked carb data.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal-linked carb data, no documented e-carb durations, and no separate activity log to explain prolonged lows.

analysis_steps.findings: Contradiction audit resolves earlier uncertainty toward keeping the current profile and automation settings unchanged for now. The strongest unresolved question is meal timing versus correction overlap; the safest next step is one clean verification window before any dependent change.
analysis_steps.evidence: The authoritative aaps_profile is complete, SMB/UAM and dynamic sensitivity are internally consistent, and the low/high patterns are real but still confounded by absent carb logs and correction-heavy response windows.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on all prior stages and the package-level authority of aaps_profile over any inferred history.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No isolated fasting window, no carb logging, and no clean meal-response dataset to justify dependent parameter changes.

strengths: CGM coverage was strong, with no invalid or duplicate entries and only short gaps.
The selected AAPS profile is complete and authoritative for review.
SMB/UAM and dynamic sensitivity are internally coherent and not obviously misconfigured.
Local-time glucose patterns are clear enough to show a real day-night structure.
No single safety-limit setting appears clearly binding or obviously unsafe from the observed range.
issues: Recurrent hypoglycemia risk is the main safety issue, especially overnight and late evening.
Sustained daytime hyperglycemia appears from late morning through afternoon.
No carb entries are available, so meal and bolus strategy cannot be validated per meal.
Therapy response windows are heavily confounded by correction boluses, SMB/UAM, IOB, temp targets, and possible site or activity effects.

recommendations.title: Keep the basal profile unchanged and verify with one fasting-style observation
recommendations.description: Overnight lows and daytime highs are both present, but the current record cannot isolate basal from meal, correction, or automation effects. Keeping the basal schedule unchanged avoids dependent edits before a clean test.

suggested_change.verification: Run one isolated fasting-style window, ideally overnight or late evening, before considering any basal adjustment.

recommendations.title: Keep SMB/UAM and dynamic sensitivity unchanged for now
recommendations.description: The SMB/UAM and sensitivity configuration is coherent, and the data do not show a material setting defect. Changing these settings now would mix automation edits with unresolved basal and meal questions.

suggested_change.verification: Review again after meal logging and a clean fasting observation; do not adjust SMB settings at the same time as basal.

recommendations.title: Defer meal-bolus changes until meals are logged clearly
recommendations.description: No carb entries are available, so any prebolus or immediate-bolus change would be speculative. Meal strategy should be reviewed only after a few documented meals with carb amounts and bolus timing.

suggested_change.verification: Log carb amount, bolus timing, and 4-6 hours of CGM for a small set of meals before changing prebolus or bolus split.

profile_recommendation.rationale: The profile shows real overnight/late-evening lows and daytime highs, but the pattern is still confounded by missing carb logs, corrections, SMB/UAM, and possible activity or site effects. A basal change is therefore not yet supported without a cleaner verification window.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Review one overnight fasting-style stretch without food, corrections, or temporary-target changes to see whether the 00:00-02:00 lows persist.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the current basal profile unchanged for now and verify it with one isolated fasting-style observation before considering any basal edit.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight lows are present, but basal cannot be isolated from correction, SMB/UAM, or missing meal data. The evidence is not strong enough to support a change to this segment alone.

Early-morning glucose is low enough at times to demand caution, yet the timing overlaps with other insulin effects and no fasting-only test is available. Changing this segment now would be speculative.
This segment may contribute to morning control, but the daytime pattern also shows meal and automation confounding. There is no isolated evidence that this basal step is wrong.
Late-morning highs exist, but they are more plausibly meal or timing related than basal-only. Without carb logs or fasting data, a basal change is not supported.
Late-afternoon lows and highs both occur in this region, but corrections, IOB, and temp targets make attribution uncertain. The evidence does not isolate this as a basal defect.
Evening lows are a concern, but the observed lows coincide with confounders and do not prove excessive basal. Keeping the segment unchanged is safer until a cleaner check is available.
The evening window contains both lows and later recovery periods, so the pattern is not clean enough for a basal edit. Dependent changes should wait until meal and correction effects are separated.
No carb entries are available, so CR cannot be validated per meal. The observed glucose pattern is too confounded to justify changing the overnight ratio.
Morning control may reflect meal timing, prebolus, or basal interactions rather than CR alone. The record does not provide enough meal-linked evidence for a supported change.
Midday highs could tempt a stronger ratio, but the package lacks carb logs and includes automation confounding. Changing this would be dependent and unsupported.
Late-day excursions are mixed, and the record cannot separate meal composition, timing, or SMB/UAM effects. There is insufficient evidence to alter this ratio now.
Evening response windows are too confounded by correction insulin and IOB to validate this ratio. A meal-linked dataset would be needed before a change is justified.
The correction response windows are mixed and do not isolate static sensitivity cleanly. Lowering or raising ISF now would mix a speculative change with unresolved automation and meal effects.
Overnight hypoglycemia is already the main safety constraint, so lowering target is not supported. Raising target might reduce lows but is not justified by a clean isolated pattern here.

Daytime hyperglycemia is present, but the package cannot show that this target is the main cause. It would be unsafe to treat it as the driver before basal, meal, and automation confounders are separated.
The late-night target is not clearly wrong, and lowering targets would increase hypoglycemia risk. No isolated evidence supports a change.
DIA cannot be isolated from SMB/UAM and correction-heavy windows, and there is no direct evidence that it is causing a mismatch. A change would be dependent and unsupported.
SMB and UAM are coherent with the observed closed-loop behavior and do not show a material configuration conflict. The data do not support changing this before resolving basal and meal questions.
The activation rules are internally consistent and do not show duplicate COB accounting or a clear safety conflict. No material inconsistency justifies changing them now.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: The observed loop behavior does not demonstrate that the interval or SMB basal limits are the source of lows or highs. The settings are plausible and should remain unchanged until cleaner data are available.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: The observed temp basal and IOB values do not approach these ceilings, so the limits do not appear to be constraining the system. The main concern is safety from lows, not a clearly too-low ceiling.
Dynamic sensitivity is active and a sensitivity_ratio near 1 is neutral, not disabled automation. No evidence shows that the sensitivity logic or target adjustment behavior is misconfigured.
There are no carb entries or extended-carb events to validate absorption settings against. Changing the model would be speculative and dependent on meal data that are not present.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Do not assign a single prebolus or immediate bolus percentage from this dataset; keep SMB/UAM unchanged, and reserve e-carbs for clearly documented prolonged or activity-related lows rather than routine meal coverage.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: There is no declared meal strategy in analysis_context and no carb logging in telemetry, so meal-specific bolus behavior cannot be validated. The observed highs and lows are real, but they remain confounded by corrections, SMB/UAM, IOB, and temporary targets.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Capture a small set of meals with exact carb amounts, bolus timing, and 4-6 hours of CGM afterward so meal timing can be separated from basal and automation effects.

exceptions.suggestion: Use e-carbs only as a separate rescue strategy, not as routine meal replacement or an extended pump bolus.
exceptions.rationale: The dataset shows low-risk periods but no direct evidence for routine e-carbs, so this should remain a rescue-only tool.

implementation_steps: First verify the current profile unchanged with one clean fasting-style observation, ideally overnight or in a low-confounder window.
Then review automation unchanged; keep SMB/UAM and dynamic sensitivity as-is until the basal question is clearer.
After that, collect a few meal-linked observations with carb amounts and bolus timing before discussing any CR, prebolus, or bolus-split change.
Reassess only after the new clean data separate meal effects from correction and basal effects; do not change dependent settings together.
education: High time-in-range can coexist with important lows; safety depends on both ends of the glucose range.
A sensitivity_ratio around 1 is a neutral current adjustment, not evidence that sensitivity automation is disabled.
Without carb logs, it is hard to tell whether a rise or fall is due to meal timing, basal, correction insulin, or SMB/UAM.
E-carbs are a separate rescue tool and should not be treated as the same thing as a pump extended bolus.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only; verify any change independently and with your usual care workflow.
Make only one change at a time and monitor CGM closely after each change.
Because lows are present, avoid tightening insulin-delivery settings without a clean verification window.
Do not change basal, CR, ISF, and automation settings together when the evidence is still confounded.
